extra.message: Unbounded note listing on /home can exhaust resources

metadata.proof: SOURCE: /home calls get_notes_for_user(current_user.id) which executes session.query(Note).filter(...).all() without LIMIT/OFFSET. SINK: Because /notes POST allows unthrottled note creation, an attacker can create a massive number of notes and then load /home, forcing the server to load, join, and render the entire result set at once.

extra.message: Unbounded search results without LIMIT can exhaust server resources

metadata.proof: The `search_param` comes from `request.args.get('search', '')` (untrusted HTTP query parameter) and is interpolated into a SQL LIKE pattern via f-string, then executed with `.all()` without any `.limit()` clause. An attacker can supply a single `%` wildcard to return all notes, or exploit the SQL injection to dump the entire notes table, causing memory exhaustion and slow rendering.

extra.message: Registration/invite codes never expire

metadata.proof: `validate_token()` queries for a matching RegistrationCode and returns its id (line 22) without checking any expiry timestamp. The RegistrationCode model has no `created_at`, `expires_at`, or any timestamp column — only `id` and `code`. A leaked or brute-forced registration code remains valid indefinitely; there is no time-based expiration mechanism.
